messages:
Sam R: Heads-up — negotiation with CedarPay is happening today. They want aggressive p95 (<=120ms) but sales asked for p99 <=400ms. Need proposal that keeps throughput for their peak QPS.
Jia L: TL;DR: we can hit p95 easily by microbatch=1/2 + fast kernels, but p99 spikes from cold KV and kernel fallback.
Leo: I ran a profile on their test fleet (10k QPS synth). Baseline (master): p50=35ms p95=95ms p99=420ms tail=900ms. The p99 is noisy.
Olivia (sales): CedarPay will pay for dedicated if we can promise 95/400. They asked for hard SLAs. Is that realistic without huge cost bump? :thinking_face:
Maya (product): We need a decision that we can document in the SOW. What's the proposed runbook for tail events?
Jia L: Quick idea: two-tier routing + tail-buffering window. Route primary to fast-gemm kernels with microbatch=2, fallback route to high-quant-stable kernel but with prewarmed KV for high QPS customers.
Sam R: Can you paste configs and perf delta? Sales wants numbers not theory.
Leo: Paste from the profiling run (condensed):
```
config A (baseline): microbatch=4 max_delay_ms=12 kernel=auto kv_warmup=false
p50 35ms p95 95ms p99 420ms tail 900ms

config B (fast-first): microbatch=2 max_delay_ms=6 kernel=fast-gemm then fallback stable-quant kv_warmup=true
p50 30ms p95 110ms p99 360ms tail 520ms

config C (single-req): microbatch=1 max_delay_ms=0 kernel=fast-gemm kv_warmup=true
p50 28ms p95 125ms p99 330ms tail 480ms
```
Jia L: Notes: config B increases p95 slightly vs baseline but drops p99 and tail a lot by avoiding heavy fallback during bursts; KV warmup halved tail.
Olivia (sales): So config B would meet p99=360ms — under 400ms target — but p95 goes to 110ms (still under 120ms). What's throughput hit?
Leo: Throughput estimated: baseline sustain 14k RPS per GPU, config B ~11k, config C ~8k. So cost delta ~ +30% for B, +75% for C.
Maya (product): Product wants minimal price impact. Can we try an adaptive microbatching policy to keep throughput but only tighten microbatch during tail events?
Jia L: Yes — propose adaptive policy: default microbatch=4, but if per-shard queue latency > Xms or tail estimator triggers, switch to microbatch=1 for that route for 30s. Also aggressive KV prefetch for that customer.
Sam R: Will adaptive switching itself add jitter? control loop needs hysteresis. We should simulate.
Leo: I ran a short sim: adaptive policy drops p95 from 95ms -> 105ms, p99 -> 380ms, throughput ~12k. Good balance.
Olivia (sales): CedarPay legal will want rollback plan. If we ship adaptive and it oscillates, they'll be unhappy. Need runbook: thresholds, escalation, opt-out.
Maya (product): Draft runbook idea: 1) pre-warm KV on deployment and high QPS windows 2) enable adaptive microbatching with conservative hysteresis 3) monitor p95/p99 and auto-fallback to config C if p99>450ms for >3min 4) alert on any kernel fallback >2% of tokens.
Sam R: Can eng commit to building hysteresis + per-tenant kernel routing? Estimate?
Jia L: Implementation pieces: metrics + controller (~2w), per-tenant config hooks (~1w), KV prewarm tweaks (~1w), sim+QA (~1w). Total ~5w, plus 1w rollout.
Olivia (sales): Timeline acceptable. Can we give CedarPay phased SLOs? E.g., Month1 commit p95<=120ms, Month3 target p99<=400ms once we finish adaptive rollout?
Maya (product): That sounds reasonable — reduces risk and gives us time to tune.
Leo: One more datapoint: regression alert earlier today from deploy-bot — kernel swap in prod increased p99 by ~60ms on a different customer with similar profile. We should include that signal in negotiation.
deploy-bot: [alert] 1901234000 kernel-swap: p99 +60ms on shard 7, auto-rolled-back, incident created #INC-792.
Sam R: OK. Action items: Jia/Led (eng) simulate adaptive + hysteresis and produce perf matrix for CedarPay load profile by EOD Friday. Leo add regression examples to packet for sales. Maya draft phased SLOs and runbook. Olivia prepare SOW draft with phased SLOs.
Olivia (sales): Thanks — I'll tell CedarPay we have a plan and the phased guarantee. :thumbsup:
Jia L: I'll post the config templates and sim output in this thread when ready.
Sam R: Great. Short log lines and simple graphs please. Keep the SLO wording conservative.
Maya (product): Also include explicit opt-out for dedicated kernel swapping in the SOW for CedarPay.
Leo: noted. I'll attach perf traces and flamegraphs to the packet once QA finishes.
Sam R: Closing loop — follow-ups in this thread. If anyone spins up experiments tag me.
